Purpose and scope

This policy sets out Alderbridge Care Group's overarching standard for recruiting and selecting staff fairly,

above the Safer Recruitment Guidance's own practical, stage-by-stage detail.

Policy statement

Alderbridge recruits on merit, against the genuine requirements of the role, within a process designed to
be fair to every candidate and safe for the people Alderbridge supports, now including a formal fast-track
route for internal mobility and promotion.

Definitions

**Person specification** the essential and desirable criteria a candidate is assessed against for a given
role. **Values-based question bank** the standard set of interview questions probing a candidate's
alignment with Alderbridge's core values. **Internal mobility fast-track** the new, formal process
introduced in this version for an existing staff member applying for internal promotion or lateral movement.
**Extended recruitment timescale** widening the standard timescale for a hard-to-fill role, now requiring
HR Director sign-off rather than the hiring manager's own discretion.

Roles and responsibilities

**The hiring manager** owns their own vacancy from person specification through to onboarding, and
must now obtain HR Director sign-off before widening the recruitment timescale for a hard-to-fill role, a
tightening from the previous version's discretion. **HR** administers the new internal mobility fast-track
process and compiles diversity monitoring data quarterly. **The HR Director** approves or declines a
request to extend a recruitment timescale, a new gate introduced in this version.

Safer Recruitment Guidance.

9. Confirm the offer as unconditional only once every required check has been satisfactorily completed.

Safer Recruitment: Manager Guidance Notes

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes support every hiring manager at Alderbridge Care Group in recruiting safely, fairly and consistently, expanding on the Recruitment and Selection Policy's own overarching standard with the practical detail a hiring manager needs at each stage of the process. They apply to every recruitment for a role with any level of contact with people supported, and in modified form to every other Alderbridge role.

Policy statement

Safer recruitment is not a single check completed once at the end of a hiring process; it is a discipline applied at every stage, from how a job is advertised through to a new starter's supervised first weeks, because the people Alderbridge supports are often less able than most to protect themselves if a genuinely unsuitable person is ever recruited into a caring role.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the highest level of criminal record check available for a role involving regulated activity with adults, required before an unsupervised start in a care-facing role. **DBS Update Service** an optional service allowing faster verification of an existing DBS certificate's continued validity between full rechecks. **Regulated activity** the specific category of work with adults at risk that legally requires an enhanced DBS check. **Interim risk assessment** a documented, time-limited arrangement allowing a supervised start pending a DBS certificate, used only where the registered manager has assessed it as genuinely safe to do so.

Roles and responsibilities

**The hiring manager** leads shortlisting, interviewing and reference requests for their own vacancy. **HR** verifies every check (DBS, references, right to work) is genuinely completed before confirming a start date, and holds the master safer recruitment checklist for every hire. **At least one interview panel member** has completed safer recruitment training within the last 3 years, per the wider Recruitment and Selection Policy. **The registered manager** authorises, and takes personal responsibility for, any interim risk assessment permitting a supervised start pending DBS.

Extended worked example: a complaint that reveals a wider issue

A worked example illustrates a complaint acting as an early warning of something more systemic than the individual complainant realised. A family member complains that their relative at Oakfield Lodge seemed unusually drowsy on several recent visits. The registered manager's investigation, prompted by this single complaint, uncovers that a recent medication review had increased a dose without the change being clearly flagged to day staff on the MAR chart summary sheet, a genuine near-system-failure the family member could not have known the specifics of, only observed the effect of. The complaint response is honest about this finding, the specific medication issue is corrected immediately, a Medication Error Report Form is separately raised to capture the system gap, and the underlying MAR chart summary sheet format is reviewed across all sites as a direct consequence — illustrating why every complaint is investigated properly rather than assumed to be simply a matter of managing the complainant's perception.

A final word for hiring managers under pressure

On the day a rota gap feels urgent and a strong candidate is waiting, remember that every safeguard in this guidance exists because, somewhere, a shortcut like the one you might be tempted to take led to real harm to a real person — that is not meant to alarm you, only to explain plainly why the extra day or two this process sometimes costs is a cost Alderbridge has decided, deliberately and permanently, is always worth paying, and no hiring manager will ever be criticised for taking the extra time this guidance asks for, whatever the rota pressure of the moment might otherwise suggest, and any manager who feels that pressure acutely should raise it with HR rather than absorb it silently and cut a corner alone, since HR would always rather help solve a genuine staffing crisis than discover afterward that a safeguard was quietly skipped by someone who felt they had no other option at the time and simply needed a better one offered to them sooner, which is exactly what raising it with HR directly and promptly actually provides, every single time it is genuinely needed, without exception, without judgement, and without any lasting mark whatsoever against the manager who simply asked for that help in good, appropriate time and with an open, honest account of the actual staffing pressure driving the request.

Final closing statement

This guidance exists so that speed and safety are never genuinely in tension when Alderbridge is filling a care-facing vacancy, because following it properly, every time, is always the faster path to a safe, sustainable hire in the end.

This policy works alongside the Safer Recruitment Guidance (the same DBS standard applies), the Safe Administration of Medication Policy and Controlled Drugs Procedure (governing the medication restriction this version adds), and the Mandatory Training Matrix (defining which training an agency worker must hold before administering medication).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the new medication restriction in practice. An agency proposes a worker for a shift at Harbour View who holds a controlled drugs qualification from their home organisation. Frequently asked questions

**Why was verbal confirmation removed as an option?** A review found verbal-only bookings occasionally led to unclear expectations about which checks had actually been completed; requiring written confirmation for every booking closes that gap. **Can the same trusted agency worker cover multiple shifts without repeating checks each time?** Yes, provided their DBS and training status remain current and confirmed. **What if an urgent gap arises with no time to email a confirmation first?** The booking is still confirmed by email, even if sent slightly after a verbal agreement to proceed — the written record requirement is not waived, only its timing may be tightly compressed in a genuine emergency.

Shift leads booking agency staff complete brief training on the verification steps this policy requires, updated to reflect the written-confirmation and medication-restriction changes in this version.

Monitoring and compliance

Agency usage volume and any related incident or concern is reviewed quarterly by HR alongside the wider Mandatory Training Matrix compliance data, with specific attention to confirming the medication restriction is being applied consistently since its introduction.

Record keeping and retention

Agency booking and verification records, including the written confirmation this version requires, are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Probation is a genuine, two-way assessment period: Alderbridge assesses whether the new starter is settling well and meeting the role's requirements, and the new starter assesses whether the role and Alderbridge are right for them, with support and honest feedback flowing in both directions throughout.

Definitions

Statement. Race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation are each protected in recruitment, employment and care delivery alike, and a resident's own view is never used to justify discriminatory treatment of a member of staff on any of these grounds, even where the resident's view reflects a genuinely held but discriminatory personal belief.

Handling a resident's discriminatory request in practice

Where a resident expresses a discriminatory preference about who provides their care, the registered manager discusses this sensitively with the resident directly, explaining Alderbridge's position, and considers whether the underlying need behind the request (for example, a genuine same-sex-carer preference for intimate personal care, which is a legitimate dignity consideration) can be met without discriminating against staff on a protected characteristic; where the request is simply discriminatory with no such legitimate underlying need, it is not accommodated, and the conversation with the resident and, where relevant, their family is recorded in their care plan so the position is consistent across every shift and every member of staff involved in their care.

Appendix: reasonable adjustments in recruitment

This appendix illustrates common reasonable adjustments made during Alderbridge recruitment, for hiring managers unfamiliar with the range of what might be requested. A candidate with dyslexia may be given extra time for a written exercise, or the option to complete it verbally instead, agreed in advance rather than raised as a surprise on the day. A candidate with a hearing impairment may be offered a British Sign Language interpreter or a written transcript of interview questions in advance. A candidate with a mobility impairment is offered step-free interview access at every Alderbridge site, confirmed in the invitation itself rather than left for the candidate to ask about. A candidate managing a mental health condition may request a shorter interview with scheduled breaks. None of these adjustments are treated as exceptional accommodations requiring special justification once genuinely requested — hiring managers are trained to expect and normalise such requests as an ordinary part of running a fair process.

A worked example illustrates a genuinely difficult overlap. A resident's family member submits a SAR while a safeguarding investigation involving that same family member is ongoing. Before any SAR response is sent, a second person (not the person who prepared it) reviews it specifically for redaction completeness and factual accuracy, since a redaction mistake in a SAR response is itself a personal data breach under the Personal Data Breach Procedure, and this second check is a control specifically designed to prevent that particular failure mode.

Occasionally a SAR-like request concerns a child rather than an adult data subject — for example, where a resident's grandchild's details appear in a visiting log; a request made on a child's behalf by a parent is assessed for the parent's own valid authority in the same way as any other third-party request, and the Data Protection Lead seeks specialist advice where the request's scope or the family circumstances are genuinely unclear.

Approval and review history

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

Working with family members who hold Lasting Power of Attorney

Where a family member holds a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare, or for property and financial affairs, staff confirm the specific scope of that authority before relying on it, since an attorney's authority is decision-specific to the type of LPA registered and does not automatically extend to every decision about the person, and Alderbridge keeps a copy of the registered document on file rather than relying on the family member's own description of their authority.

When a decision genuinely cannot wait

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.
